summary: This tutorial covers how to use JChemPaint, a chemical structures editor, on Ubuntu Linux OS version 12.04 with Java version 7. It starts by welcoming users to the tutorial and explaining that they will learn about periodic table trends, creating reactions, and setting up R-group queries. The tutorial walks through opening the JChemPaint window using the terminal command `java -jar jchempaint331210.jar`. It then guides users through adding elements to the periodic table, selecting elements via keyboard or the periodic table button, and viewing detailed information about selected elements. Users can also type element symbols directly into the text box and create chemical structures like xenon difluoride (XeF2). The tutorial explains how to access preferences to show implicit hydrogens and change element properties, including isotopes and element features such as alkali earth metals.
